content.text: The text discusses cancerous peritonitis, emphasizing ovarian scirrhous carcinoma with secondary peritoneal, gastric, duodenal, tubal, and lymph-node deposits. It contrasts cancerous with tuberculous peritonitis and describes palliative treatment. Infantile peritonitis is reviewed, including congenital, syphilitic, and septic forms. A major section examines ascites: causes—especially portal obstruction and liver disease—clinical signs, differential diagnosis from ovarian cysts, and treatment with diuretics, diaphoretics, purgatives, and paracentesis. Hemorrhagic peritoneal effusion is also considered. Tabes mesenterica is defined as tuberculosis of mesenteric glands, with emphasis on childhood incidence, causes, pathology, symptoms, diagnosis, poor prognosis, prevention, and nutritional palliation. The remainder is an extensive alphabetical index of abdominal and systemic diseases, symptoms, pathology, and treatments. Sandra went to the bathroom; Mary went to the office.
